sections.content:
31,125 people

were counted on the census as "quantity surveyors" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Quantity surveyors advise on financial and contractual matters relating to, and prepare bills of quantities for, construction projects and provide other support functions concerning the financing and materials required for building projects.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "quantity surveyors" there were more men than women (84.1% compared with 15.9%).

This means "quantity surveyors" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 84.1% and women made up 15.9% of "quantity surveyors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "quantity surveyors" included:

  • engineering professionals (other)
  • plastics process operatives
  • programmers and software development professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "quantity surveyors", 18% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "quantity surveyors" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "quantity surveyors" included:

  • dancers and choreographers
  • actors, entertainers and presenters
  • pensions and insurance clerks and assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "quantity surveyors" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "quantity surveyors" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "quantity surveyors", 4.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (93% compared with 7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (86.4%) than self-employed (13.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
